You are a repo feature worker. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the loop-factory repository, detached at HEAD. Edit files here directly.

OWNERSHIP: you own exactly two paths, factory/reescalate.py (new) and tests/test_reescalate.py (new). Do NOT modify, create, delete, or reformat anything else under factory/, tests/, kernel/, runbooks/, departments/, or loopfactory.py. Do NOT git commit, do NOT git push, do NOT run git add -A. Leave your changes uncommitted; the check exports them.

CONTEXT. loop-factory routes anything a department cannot decide to its owner as a Linear card plus a Telegram prompt with Approve/Respond buttons. Those Telegram buttons carry a nonce that expires after 72 hours, but the Linear card never expires. The owner explicitly may take days to answer. So the system must re-ping him before the buttons go dead, and must never stop nagging. That re-ping is what you are building.

READ FIRST, READ-ONLY, for conventions: factory/outbox_push.py (writes the ledger rows you will read), factory/outbox_listen.py (reads the same ledger; see _open_groups for how rows are grouped by card_identifier), tests/test_outbox_listen.py (test style), CLAUDE.md (repo rules).

THE LEDGER YOU READ is JSONL, one JSON object per line, append-only, last row per row_hash wins. Relevant fields: row_hash, card_identifier, status, first_raised (ISO 8601), urgency ('normal' or 'urgent'), due (ISO 8601, present when urgent), last_ping_at (ISO 8601, absent until you have pinged once), reescalation_count (integer, absent means 0). Several ledger rows routinely share one card_identifier because the card creator dedupes by content; production had 36 rows on 13 cards, one card carrying 13 rows.

BUILD factory/reescalate.py with this exact CLI:
  python3 factory/reescalate.py --ledger <path> --now <iso8601> --plan-only
It must print a JSON object to stdout: {"due": [{"card_identifier": str, "reescalation_count": int, "reason": str}, ...]} naming exactly the cards owed a ping at that instant. --plan-only must be pure: read the ledger, print, write nothing and send nothing.

CADENCE RULES, these are the product:
1. Only cards whose latest ledger row has status 'open' or 'fix_requested' are eligible. Any other status, including 'retired', 'decided:approve' and 'decided:skip', is never re-escalated.
2. Group by card_identifier. Exactly ONE ping is owed per card per tick no matter how many ledger rows share it.
3. The clock starts at last_ping_at, or at first_raised when there has been no ping.
4. urgency 'normal': the interval is 48 hours for the first three pings (reescalation_count 0, 1, 2), then doubles for each subsequent ping, capped at 336 hours. It never stops.
5. urgency 'urgent' (has a due date): the interval is half the time remaining from the clock start to due, with a hard floor of 2 hours. Once past due, the interval is 2 hours.
6. A card is due when now is at or after clock start plus interval.

WHY 48 HOURS MATTERS: the Telegram nonce dies at 72 hours. A normal card must always be re-pinged before that or the owner's buttons stop working. Do not let any normal interval exceed 72 hours before the first re-ping.

ALSO SUPPORT a send mode: without --plan-only, the module must send each due ping through an argv template supplied by config, exactly the way factory/outbox_push.py renders its senders (a list of strings with placeholders, never a shell string), then append a ledger row per pinged card recording the new last_ping_at and incremented reescalation_count, keeping status unchanged. Do NOT hardcode Telegram, Linear, or any transport. A missing or unusable sender config must fail closed with a printed reason and a nonzero exit, never a silent success.

WRITE tests/test_reescalate.py covering the cadence rules above, following the subprocess style used in tests/test_outbox_listen.py. Your tests are not the acceptance gate; an independent oracle drives your CLI through fixtures you have not seen.

VERIFY before you finish, from the worktree root:
  PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider
The whole suite must stay green; it was 671 passing before you started.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: leave factory/reescalate.py and tests/test_reescalate.py edited and uncommitted, and write ./notes.md at the ROOT of your worktree (the check copies it out before the worktree is deleted, and it is not a repo file so it will not trip the ownership gate) recording what you read, the cadence decisions you made, the verification command you ran and its result, and any assumption.

HARD RULES: keep it boring and local to existing patterns. No new dependencies. No network. No Telegram or Linear calls. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. Do not capture anything to any memory or brain service. If something is ambiguous, state the assumption in ./notes.md rather than widening your ownership.
tasks.verified: an independent oracle drove factory/reescalate.py --plan-only through 13 unseen cadence fixtures (early/late normal, 72h TTL invariant, backoff doubling and 336h cap, urgent half-remaining and 2h floor, past-due, retired, decided, and one-ping-per-shared-card), the full 671-test suite still passes, only owned files changed, and the patch was exported outside the worktree.

CONTEXT. Every loop-factory department needs a way to reach its human owner: an escalation it writes to departments/<name>/state/decisions_outbox.jsonl is picked up by a watcher process, turned into a Linear card, and buzzed to the owner's phone. That watcher reads a single YAML config whose 'watches' list names each department's outbox. Today a department only gets wired up if someone remembers to hand-edit that config, and one department's escalations sat undelivered because nobody did. Your job is to make the wiring automatic at scaffold time so it cannot be forgotten.

READ FIRST, READ-ONLY, for conventions: factory/outbox_push.py (owns the config schema; note the module constant KINDS and the load_config validator, which is strict and fails closed), factory/scaffold.py (what you are extending), runbooks/factory-pipeline.md (the F0 to F6 pipeline you are documenting into), CLAUDE.md (repo rules, especially that factory code must never contain a department name).

BUILD factory/mailroom_registry.py with this exact CLI:
  python3 factory/mailroom_registry.py --config <path> --department <name> --outbox <path>
Behaviour:
1. Add one watch entry {path, department, kind} to the config's 'watches' list. The kind must be a value factory/outbox_push.py's KINDS accepts.
2. Idempotent. Registering the same department and outbox twice must leave exactly ONE entry, and the second call must still exit 0.
3. Never disturb anything else in the config. cursor_file, ledger_file, senders and listener must come back byte-equivalent in meaning.
4. Fail closed. A config that is missing, unreadable, or not a YAML mapping must exit nonzero AND print why. A silent success on a broken config is the exact defect this repo exists to prevent.
5. Write atomically, the way factory/human_in_the_loop.py does, so a crash mid-write cannot corrupt the operator's config.

WIRE IT IN: factory/scaffold.py must call the registry when it scaffolds a department, registering departments/<name>/state/decisions_outbox.jsonl. The config path must be overridable (argument or environment variable) so tests never touch the operator's real config, and scaffolding must not hard-fail when the config is absent on a fresh machine, though it must say so out loud.

DOCUMENT IT: add the mailroom wiring to runbooks/factory-pipeline.md as a named step, and add it to the 'Definition of done for a stood department' list. Use the word 'mailroom'. Keep the existing document's voice and structure.

WRITE tests/test_mailroom_registry.py covering the five behaviours above using tmp_path, following the style of the existing tests. Your tests are not the acceptance gate; an independent oracle drives your CLI through fixtures you have not seen.

VERIFY before you finish, from the worktree root:
  PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider
The whole suite must stay green; it was 671 passing before you started.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: leave the four owned files edited and uncommitted, and write ./notes.md at the ROOT of your worktree (the check copies it out before the worktree is deleted, and it is not a repo file so it will not trip the ownership gate) recording what you read, what you changed, the verification command and its result, and any assumption.

HARD RULES: no department name may appear in factory/ code. No new dependencies. No network. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. Do not capture anything to any memory or brain service. State assumptions in notes.md rather than widening your ownership.

Do NOT modify, create, delete, or reformat anything else under factory/, tests/, kernel/, runbooks/, departments/, or loopfactory.py. In particular do NOT touch factory/outbox_listen.py; another worker owns adjacent files this round. Do NOT git commit, do NOT git push, do NOT run git add -A. Leave your changes uncommitted; the check exports them.

CONTEXT, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE POINT. factory/outbox_push.py watches a list of files named in its config and turns new lines into Linear cards plus a phone notification for the owner. On 2026-08-02 its config was edited so that the only path it watched no longer existed. For six days the timer fired every fifteen minutes, found nothing, and exited 0. Every dashboard was green while the human approval channel was completely dead. Nobody noticed. You are building the sensor that makes that impossible.

READ FIRST, READ-ONLY, for conventions: factory/outbox_push.py (the file you are changing; note tick(), the existing exit code 3 for a total ping-sender failure, and ConfigError with exit 2), tests/test_outbox_push.py (test style and the existing exit-code expectations), CLAUDE.md (repo rules, especially rule 2, deny by default, and the ban on allow-on-failure paths).

BUILD THIS BEHAVIOUR:
1. A tick in which EVERY configured watch path is missing from disk is a stall, not a success. Exit with a distinct nonzero code and print a message that names the missing path or paths, so the operator can fix it without reading the source.
2. A tick in which AT LEAST ONE configured watch path exists is not a stall, even if that file is empty and there is nothing to push. It must still exit 0. An idle mailroom is healthy; a blind one is not.
3. --dry-run must keep its current meaning and must not be turned into a stall failure by your change.
4. Choose an exit code that does not collide with the existing meanings (2 is config error, 3 is total send failure). Document the code you chose in the module docstring alongside the others.
5. Do not weaken or reorder any existing behaviour: cursor and row-hash dedup, the ledger append, the ping-then-card ordering, and the existing exit 3 path must all still work exactly as they do now.

WRITE tests/test_outbox_push_stall.py, covering: all-paths-missing exits nonzero and names a missing path; one-path-present-and-empty exits 0; dry-run is unaffected. Follow the subprocess style in tests/test_outbox_push.py. Your tests are not the acceptance gate; an independent oracle drives the CLI through fixtures you have not seen.

VERIFY before you finish, from the worktree root:
  PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider
The whole suite must stay green; it was 671 passing before you started. If an existing test in tests/test_outbox_push.py now fails because it configured a watch path that does not exist, that is a real signal: do not delete or weaken the test, make the fixture create the file it claims to watch.

HARD RULES: never add an allow-on-failure path. No new dependencies. No network. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. Do not capture anything to any memory or brain service. State assumptions in notes.md rather than widening your ownership.
